patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — RingCentral documents a broader use-case set; Slack is narrower/specialist.

General-purpose vs specialist. Choose RingCentral only if your buying job matches “Enterprise-grade UCaaS / cloud phone platform (RingEX) with deep call routing, video, team” rather than Slack's shape. Choose Slack only if your buying job matches “Channel-based team messaging platform — Free $0, Pro $7.25/user/month annual, Business+ $1” rather than RingCentral's shape. Workflow advantage: RingCentral leans business-phone, sales-calling; Slack leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — RingCentral documents a broader use-case set; Slack is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: RingCentral is Enterprise-grade UCaaS / cloud phone platform (RingEX) with deep call routing, video, team messaging and contact-centre options — Core from ; Slack is Channel-based team messaging platform — Free $0, Pro $7.25/user/month annual, Business+ $15, Enterprise+ contact sales; huddles for light vi.
- Company-size focus: RingCentral (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Slack (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: RingCentral-leaning business-phone, sales-calling, contact-center vs Slack-leaning —.
- Researched limits: RingCentral — Published seat floors are medium confidence — RingCentral often gates exact dollars behind quote/selector flows; Slack — Not a business phone system — no cloud phone, call routing, recording or power dialer.

Limitations — RingCentral: Published seat floors are medium confidence — RingCentral often gates exact dollars behind quote/selector flows; Call recording and deeper CRM/CTI require Advanced or above; Slack: Not a business phone system — no cloud phone, call routing, recording or power dialer; No SMS or WhatsApp Business customer channels.

Poor-fit cases: RingCentral is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Published seat floors are medium confidence — RingCentral often gates exact dollars behind quote/selector flows · Slack is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a business phone system — no cloud phone, call routing, recording or power dialer · Avoid RingCentral if you actually need Slack's motion (Channel-based team messaging platform — Free $0, Pro $7.25/user/month annual, Bu)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
